title: Intercalation Engineering of Ferroic Properties in 2D Materials
summary: Using molecular and atomic intercalation to control magnetic ordering and switchable polarization in layered materials.
advisors: Prof. Changzheng Wu and Prof. Yuqiao Guo
motivation: The interlayer space in transition-metal dichalcogenides offers a route to modify symmetry and interfacial coupling. This project examines whether molecular and atomic guests can induce ferroic behavior in layered hosts.
contributions: Grew TaS₂ single crystals and synthesized cobaltocene-intercalated TaS₂. Used structural and magnetic measurements to check intercalation and characterize the resulting materials.
Proposed site-selective Cu intercalation in TaS₂, synthesized Cu-intercalated samples, performed piezoresponse force microscopy, and used VASP to investigate stable interlayer configurations.
methods: Chemical vapor transport and solvothermal intercalation
X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, vibrating-sample magnetometry, and magnetic force microscopy
Piezoresponse force microscopy and first-principles structural optimization in VASP
results: The published molecular-intercalation study reports room-temperature ferromagnetism in a family of layered materials.

In the ongoing Cu-intercalation study, I observed ferroelectric switching and domain writing by piezoresponse force microscopy. Calculations identified two energetically stable interlayer sites. I am exploring how the approach extends to other transition-metal dichalcogenides.

title: In Situ PLD-EIS for Oxygen Exchange Kinetics
summary: Tracking how PrOₓ surface decoration affects oxygen exchange on LSCF electrodes during thin-film experiments.
motivation: Surface chemistry influences oxygen exchange at oxide electrodes. Combining pulsed laser deposition and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy makes it possible to monitor electrochemical changes within the deposition chamber.
contributions: Helped build and optimize a PLD system with integrated real-time EIS.
Measured LSCF electrodes with and without PrOₓ surface modification under anodic and cathodic bias and analyzed concentration-amended activation energies.
methods: In situ pulsed laser deposition with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
Biased oxygen-exchange measurements on decorated and undecorated LSCF
results: The analysis indicated a lower activation barrier for PrOₓ-decorated LSCF under the conditions studied. Quantitative plots and experimental details can be added when available.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted TEM Analysis of Nanocrystal Superlattices
summary: Mapping subtle structural variations in TEM images using local Fourier fingerprints and unsupervised learning.
motivation: Subtle changes in nanocrystal packing can be difficult to distinguish by eye in transmission electron microscopy. Local Fourier analysis provides spatially resolved descriptors for comparing structure across an image.
contributions: Developed and implemented a Python workflow that extracts local TEM image patches, builds FFT-based fingerprints, reduces dimensionality, and clusters the results with Gaussian mixture models.
methods: Local fast Fourier transform fingerprints and dimensionality reduction
Gaussian mixture clustering and phase-map reconstruction
results: The workflow produced spatially resolved phase maps for identifying subtle structural variation, phase boundaries, and heterogeneity. The software was registered for copyright at Brown University, and a manuscript is in preparation.

title: Single-Atom-Modified Quantum Dots for Coupled Photocatalysis
summary: Investigating Au and Pd single-atom sites on CdS/ZnS quantum dots for coupled CO₂ reduction and organic oxidation.
motivation: Coupling CO₂ reduction with organic oxidation gives photogenerated electrons and holes separate reaction pathways. This work investigates how isolated metal sites might promote the two half-reactions.
contributions: Synthesized Au- and Pd-single-atom-modified CdS/ZnS quantum dots, assessed photocatalytic activity by gas chromatography, and characterized alcohol oxidation products with NMR spectroscopy.
methods: Synthesis of single-atom-modified CdS/ZnS quantum dots
Photocatalytic activity measurements and gas chromatography
results: The roles of Au and Pd in the two half-reactions are under investigation. Performance data and mechanistic conclusions will be added when available.
